# Full 0–360° Angle Functions check {.appendix #apx-360-angle}
The primary analyses modeled angular disparity — the shortest rotational distance to upright, capped at 180° — on the assumption that participants rotate stimuli via the most efficient path. To test this assumption, we re-ran the clustering using full 0–360° rotation angles and plotted RT and accuracy functions across the complete angular range (@fig-rt-angle-by-strategy-360, @fig-accuracy-angle-by-strategy-360). We verified that the angular disparity variable was correctly computed, confirming that full rotation angles were accurately recoded to their shortest-path equivalents (e.g., a 320° rotation has a disparity of 40°).

The results were broadly consistent with the disparity-based analyses and provided direct support for the shortest-path assumption. Both the Mental Rotation and Flipping/Matching groups showed RT functions that increased from 20° to a peak around 200–240°, then declined as angles approached 320°, forming the expected near-symmetric inverted-U around 180°. This pattern is precisely what would be predicted if participants always rotate via the shorter available path, and would not be expected under a fixed-direction rotation strategy.

The flipping signature observed in the Flipping/Matching group was again evident in the full-angle data: their RT function rose more steeply than the Mental Rotation group and remained elevated through 240° before declining, consistent with a strategy that exploits reflective symmetry at high disparities. Accuracy for both effective strategy groups showed a corresponding U-shaped function, declining to a minimum around 160–200° before recovering at higher angles, with the Flipping/Matching group maintaining the highest accuracy throughout. The Ineffective Strategies group again showed a broadly decreasing RT function across the full angular range, with accuracy remaining near chance at peak angles and showing only a modest recovery above 240°, further supporting the interpretation that these children are not engaging with the spatial structure of the items.
```{r}
#| label: robustness-check-all-angles
#| results: "hide"

# Ability estimate - keep site + user
ability_user <- all_scores %>% 
  filter(item_task == "mrot", metric_type == "ability") %>% 
  mutate(
    metric_value = as.numeric(metric_value),
    age = as.numeric(age)
  ) %>%
  group_by(site, user_id) %>%
  summarise(
    ability = mean(metric_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    age     = first(age),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

mrot_rich_data <- mrot_rt_trial_no_retest %>%
  mutate(
    stimulus = str_extract(item, "^[a-z]+"),
    
    # Extract full 0-360° angle directly from item_original
    angle = as.integer(str_extract(item_original, "\\d{3}$")),
    
    # Calculate shortest distance to center (disparity) for the model
    ang_disparity = pmin(angle, 360 - angle),
    
    stimulus = as.factor(stimulus),
    angle_s  = as.numeric(scale(ang_disparity)), 
    trial_s  = as.numeric(scale(trial_number))
  )

# --- Doria's FIX: Set Sum-to-Zero Contrasts ---
# By default, R uses treatment contrasts (Duck = reference). 
# This makes the "Angle" slope represent only Ducks (which is flat for everyone).
# Setting sum contrasts ensures the "Angle" slope represents the GRAND MEAN slope across all stimuli.
contrasts(mrot_rich_data$stimulus) <- contr.sum(levels(mrot_rich_data$stimulus))
# Fit the rich mixed model
m_rich <- lmer(
  log_rt ~ angle_s * stimulus + trial_s +
    (1 + angle_s + trial_s | user_id) +
    (1 | item),
  data = mrot_rich_data,
  control = lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 20000))
)

# Extract subject-level random effects (deviations)
ran_effs <- ranef(m_rich)$user_id %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("user_id") %>%
  rename(
    int_dev   = `(Intercept)`,
    slope_dev = angle_s,
    trial_dev = trial_s
  )

# Fixed effects (global averages)
fix_int <- fixef(m_rich)["(Intercept)"]
fix_ang <- fixef(m_rich)["angle_s"]
fix_tri <- fixef(m_rich)["trial_s"]

# Compute cognitive features (on log-RT scale)
rich_features_raw <- ran_effs %>%
  mutate(
    # Baseline Speed: Speed at angle 0 (Intercept)
    Baseline_Speed = fix_int + int_dev,
    # Absolute Slope: Time added per degree of rotation (Rotation Cost)
    Abs_Slope      = fix_ang + slope_dev,
    # Relative Slope (Per Mike's suggestion)
    # "Is rotation expensive relative to their normal speed?"
    Rel_Slope      = Abs_Slope / Baseline_Speed,
    # Learning Rate 
    Learning_Rate  = fix_tri + trial_dev
  )
# 4. Compute Instability (Residual SD)
# We calculate SD of the *residuals* (not raw RT) to remove the "Task Difficulty" confound.
# This isolates internal inconsistency from the fact that some kids saw harder items.
mrot_rich_data$resid <- residuals(m_rich)

instability_data <- mrot_rich_data %>%
  group_by(site, user_id) %>%
  summarise(
    # Instability = SD of residuals (pure internal noise)
    Instability = sd(resid, na.rm = TRUE), 
    .groups = "drop"
  )

user_site_map <- mrot_rt_trial_no_retest %>%
  distinct(site, user_id)

# 5. Join and Prepare for Clustering
rich_features_final <- rich_features_raw %>%
  left_join(user_site_map, by = "user_id") %>%
  left_join(instability_data, by = c("site", "user_id")) %>% 
  left_join(ability_user,  by = c("site", "user_id")) %>%
  mutate(
    Site = str_replace_all(site, c("pilot_" = "", "_" = "-"))
  ) %>%
  # Filter to ensure all needed features are finite
  # UPDATED: Added Learning_Rate to the list
  filter(if_all(c(ability, Abs_Slope, Rel_Slope, Baseline_Speed, Instability, Learning_Rate), is.finite))

# Check: ang_disparity should never exceed 180
summary(mrot_rich_data$ang_disparity)

# Spot check a few items
mrot_rich_data %>%
  select(item, item_original, angle, ang_disparity) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(item_original) %>%
  head(20)
```

```{r}
my_colors <- c(
  "Ineffective Strategies" = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(3, "Set1")[1],

)

analysis_data <- rich_features_final %>%

  select(Baseline_Speed, Rel_Slope, Abs_Slope, 
         Instability, Learning_Rate) %>%
  scale()
set.seed(123)
k_global <- kmeans(global_input, centers = 3, nstart = 25)
analysis_data$Global_Cluster <- as.factor(k_global$cluster)
cluster_stats <- analysis_data %>%
  group_by(Global_Cluster) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_ability = mean(ability),
    mean_slope   = mean(Rel_Slope), 
    .groups = "drop"
  )
low_eff_id <- cluster_stats %>%
  arrange(mean_ability) %>% slice(1) %>% pull(Global_Cluster)
effective_clusters <- cluster_stats %>%
  filter(Global_Cluster != low_eff_id) %>%
  arrange(mean_slope)
analytical_id <- effective_clusters %>% slice(1) %>% pull(Global_Cluster)
holistic_id   <- effective_clusters %>% slice(2) %>% pull(Global_Cluster)
analysis_data <- analysis_data %>%
  mutate(Strategy_Label = case_when(
    Global_Cluster == low_eff_id    ~ "Ineffective Strategies",
    Global_Cluster == analytical_id ~ "Other Effective Strategies (Flipping/Matching)",
    Global_Cluster == holistic_id   ~ "Mental Rotation"
  ))
ggplot(analysis_data, aes(x = ability, y = Rel_Slope, color = Strategy_Label)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_manual(values = my_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "Cluster Result: Ability vs. Relative Slope (full 0-360° angles)",
    x = "Ability", y = "Relative Slope"
  )
```

```{r}
# helpers
ARI <- function(a, b) {
  a <- as.integer(factor(a))
  b <- as.integer(factor(b))
  tab <- table(a, b)
  n <- sum(tab)
  if (n <= 1) return(NA_real_)
  comb2    <- function(x) x * (x - 1) / 2
  sum_ij   <- sum(comb2(tab))
  sum_i    <- sum(comb2(rowSums(tab)))
  sum_j    <- sum(comb2(colSums(tab)))
  expected <- (sum_i * sum_j) / comb2(n)
  max_idx  <- 0.5 * (sum_i + sum_j)
  denom    <- max_idx - expected
  if (denom == 0) return(NA_real_)
  (sum_ij - expected) / denom
}

jaccard <- function(set_a, set_b) {
  inter <- length(intersect(set_a, set_b))
  uni   <- length(union(set_a, set_b))
  if (uni == 0) NA_real_ else inter / uni
}

label_order_ref[low_eff_id_ref]   <- which(ref_levels == "Ineffective Strategies")
label_order_ref[analytical_id_ref] <- which(ref_levels == "Other Effective Strategies (Flipping/Matching)")
label_order_ref[holistic_id_ref]   <- which(ref_levels == "Mental Rotation")

# ref_centers[i, ] corresponds to ref_levels[i]
ref_centers <- km_ref$centers[order(label_order_ref), , drop = FALSE]

# bootstrap loop
res <- map_dfr(1:B, function(b) {

  set.seed(1000 + b)

  idx        <- sample.int(n, size = n, replace = TRUE)
  idx_unique <- unique(idx)

  tab_ref_unique <- table(factor(y_ref[idx_unique], levels = ref_levels))
  min_ref_unique <- min(tab_ref_unique)
  min_ref_prop   <- min_ref_unique / length(idx_unique)
  n_unique       <- length(idx_unique)

  X_b <- X_full[idx, , drop = FALSE]
  km  <- kmeans(X_b, centers = k, nstart = nstart)

  # assign all full-sample participants to nearest bootstrap center
  centers_b <- km$centers
  dists <- sapply(1:k, function(j) {
    rowSums((X_full - matrix(centers_b[j, ],
                             nrow = nrow(X_full), ncol = ncol(X_full),
                             byrow = TRUE))^2)
  })
  cl_hat <- max.col(-dists)

  # resolve label switching via maximum overlap with reference labels
  perm  <- best_perm_by_overlap(cl_hat, y_ref, ref_levels, all_perms_3)
  y_hat <- factor(ref_levels[perm[cl_hat]], levels = ref_levels)

  ari <- ARI(y_ref, y_hat)

  # per-cluster Jaccard
  jac <- map_dbl(ref_levels, function(lab) {
    jaccard(ids[y_ref == lab], ids[y_hat == lab])
  })
  names(jac) <- paste0("J_", make.names(ref_levels))

  # mean centroid displacement vs reference
  centers_b_aligned <- centers_b[perm, , drop = FALSE]
  center_shift      <- mean(sqrt(rowSums((centers_b_aligned - ref_centers)^2)))

  tibble(
    replicate      = b,
    ARI            = ari,
    n_unique       = n_unique,
    min_ref_unique = min_ref_unique,
    min_ref_prop   = min_ref_prop,
    center_shift   = center_shift,
    !!!as.list(jac)
  )
})

# summaries
stability_summary <- res %>%
  summarise(
    B                   = n(),
    ARI_median          = median(ARI, na.rm = TRUE),
    ARI_IQR             = IQR(ARI, na.rm = TRUE),
    center_shift_median = median(center_shift, na.rm = TRUE),
    center_shift_IQR    = IQR(center_shift, na.rm = TRUE),
    across(starts_with("J_"),
           list(median = ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                IQR    = ~ IQR(.x, na.rm = TRUE)))
  )

stability_summary

ari_tail <- res %>%
  summarise(
    pct_ARI_below_0.70 = mean(ARI < 0.70, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    pct_ARI_below_0.60 = mean(ARI < 0.60, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    min_ARI            = min(ARI, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

ari_tail
```

####################### ROBUSTNESS CHECK - WITHIN PERSON STRATEGY SWITCHING (DORIA'S ANALYSIS) ##########################

### Strategy Stability Analysis (Split-Half Reliability)

To investigate whether children consistently use a single cognitive strategy throughout the task or switch strategies over time (e.g., discovering a shortcut), we performed a **Split-Half Reliability Analysis**.

**Methodology:**
We partitioned each participant's data into two sequential halves: the first 50% of trials (Early Phase) and the last 50% of trials (Late Phase). For each half, we estimated a "Raw Slope" using a simple linear regression of reaction time on angle (`log_rt ~ angle`). This slope serves as a proxy for the participant's rotation strategy during that specific period. 

We then correlated the *First Half Slope* with the *Second Half Slope* to quantify stability. A high correlation ($r \approx 1$) would indicate a fixed strategy, while a low correlation ($r \approx 0$) suggests dynamic behavior or strategy switching.

```{r}
#| label: fig-strategy-switching
#| fig-cap: "Strategy Stability: Comparison of Rotation Slope in First Half vs. Second Half of trials. Points below the diagonal suggest a switch to a flatter strategy (e.g., discovering the shortcut)."


# 1. Split Data into Halves
# We determine the midpoint trial for each user
split_data <- mrot_rich_data %>%
  group_by(user_id) %>%
  mutate(
    Midpoint = median(trial_number, na.rm = TRUE),
    Half = ifelse(trial_number <= Midpoint, "First_Half", "Second_Half")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  # Filter out bad data points just to be safe
  filter(is.finite(log_rt), is.finite(angle))

# 2. Calculate Simple Slope for Each Half (Using simple lm per subject)
# This is a fast proxy for the complex mixed-model slope
slope_stability <- split_data %>%
  group_by(user_id, Half) %>%
  summarise(
    # We only care about the slope (coefficient for angle)
    # We use a safe lm() call wrapped in tryCatch to handle kids with too few trials
    Raw_Slope = tryCatch(
      #coef(lm(log_rt ~ angle, data = pick(everything())))["angle"], 
      # Use distance from 0 so the slope represents 'cost of rotation'
  coef(lm(log_rt ~ pmin(angle, 360 - angle), data = pick(everything())))[2],
      error = function(e) NA_real_
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  # Reshape to Wide Format (Columns: Slope_First, Slope_Second)
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Half, values_from = Raw_Slope, names_prefix = "Slope_") %>%
  # Join with our Final Strategy Labels to color-code
  left_join(analysis_data %>% select(user_id, Strategy_Label), by = "user_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Strategy_Label), !is.na(Slope_First_Half), !is.na(Slope_Second_Half))

# 3. Calculate Correlation (Quantify Stability)
correlation <- cor(slope_stability$Slope_First_Half, slope_stability$Slope_Second_Half, use = "complete.obs")

# 4. Visualization
ggplot(slope_stability, aes(x = Slope_First_Half, y = Slope_Second_Half, color = Strategy_Label)) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray50") + # The "Stability Line"
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6, size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = my_colors) +
  labs(
    title = "Strategy Switching Check (Split-Half Reliability)",
    subtitle = paste0("Correlation between halves: r = ", round(correlation, 2), 
                      ". Points below diagonal = Strategy became flatter (faster)."),
    x = "Slope (First Half of Trials)",
    y = "Slope (Second Half of Trials)"
  ) +
  coord_fixed() # Keeps the aspect ratio square so the diagonal is 45 degrees
```

```{r}
# Doria's original code for examining up to 360 
mrot_rich_data <- mrot_rt_trial_no_retest %>%
  mutate(
    stimulus = str_extract(item, "^[a-z]+"),
    
    # 1. Extract the base angle (e.g., 40)
    base_angle = as.integer(str_extract(item, "\\d+")), 
    
    # 2. Detect if the original item was a "Negative/Counter-Clockwise" rotation
    # Looking for 'rn' prefix in item_original (e.g., rn040)
    is_ccw = str_detect(item_original, "^rn"),
    
    # 3. RECONSTRUCT the full 0-360 angle
    angle = ifelse(is_ccw, 360 - base_angle, base_angle),
    
    # 4. Calculate shortest distance to center (disparity) for the model
    # This ensures the model still measures 'Rotation Cost' correctly
    ang_disparity = pmin(angle, 360 - angle),
    
    stimulus = as.factor(stimulus),
    # SCALE THE DISPARITY, NOT THE RAW ANGLE
    angle_s  = as.numeric(scale(ang_disparity)), 
    trial_s  = as.numeric(scale(trial_number))
  )

#  Issues: the above code is only only catches rabbit counter-clockwise items (rn040, rn080 etc.), and misses duck and shape items. It is also not necessary to deconstruct item_original as the info. we need is already there. item_original already contains the full angle directly (e.g., an11240 = 240).
```
